description:
Filed s520 by s519a (ruling 4 of s519, DECIDED ## s519).  After #3370's lowerings (the void comma-list split, its logical spellings `COND and/or/&&/|| (LIST)` / `COND and/or local ...` (ruling 3), and the first-evaluated hoist), a `local` term no lowering reaches is a missing case on rule 12's s329 boundary: in a VALUE position the statement consumes, a ruled refusal at the statement; in a VOID position the old read stays -- the operand is assigned / read, NEVER localized -- and the transpile announces
  PCL: local in an unsupported expression position at F line N -- not localized
(Pl::Parser::announce_unlocalized_local; Parser2 _local_value_consumed decides the class).

THE SITE SCAN (s520, scratch/s519a/scan/scan2.pl: Parser2's _lower_local_terms run over plain-PPI documents -- the pipeline's other passes are not applied, so a shape another pass rewrites first may be counted differently):
  population            files   non-leading local sites   refuse   announce
  installed site_perl     234          3                    0        0      (Role::Tiny 307 + its two spellings now lowered)
  core lib/5.40.3        1393          7                    0        2
  lib/ (PCL shims)         50          0                    0        0
  the 19 board dists      554         14                    0        0
  perl-tests/             174         14                    1        0
The residue, every site:
  ANNOUNCE  (my $self, local $_) = @_;        ExtUtils/CBuilder/Platform/Windows.pm:74 (a Windows-only module)
  ANNOUNCE  (my $__, local $noticks) = @_;    dumpvar.pl:71
  REFUSE    @{1, local $x[0][0]} = 1;          perl-tests/multideref.t:220 (a row that already failed)
Before ruling 3's extension the scan also found `$cv and local($self->{curcv}) = $cv, local(...), local(@$self{qw'...'})` (B::Deparse 6279) and `DEBUG and local $Data::Dumper::Useqq = 1;` (YAML::PP::Emitter 508) -- both now lowered (Pl/t/local-term-01.t row 11).

THE ONE SHAPE LEFT (both announce sites): a `local` lvalue inside a list assignment's parenthesised LHS.  Perl evaluates the RHS FIRST, then localizes, then assigns, so hoisting `local $_;` before the statement is WRONG when the RHS reads the operand by name (`(local $x) = ($x)` keeps the old value).  A correct lowering: `my @t = (RHS); local OPERAND; (LHS-without-local) = @t;` (the `my` declarations of the LHS stay in the statement's scope).  Probe (5.40.3): `sub sls { (my $x, local $_) = @_; } $_ = "out"; sls(1, 2); print $_` prints `out`; PCL prints `2` and announces.  Guard: Pl/t/local-term-01.t row 13-14 (asserts the announcement and the run-on; flip it to a perl compare when this is fixed).

=== s519b (s520, Fable ruling) ===
perl-tests/multideref.t row 49 ("RT #130727 part 2: array not autovivified") left cl/skip-registry.lisp in s519b and passes ACCIDENTALLY: the multideref.t:220 refusal (this task's value-position residue) dies before the assignment runs.  RE-EXAMINE that row when :220 is lowered -- it may then fail on the RT #130727 quirk (docs/not-supported.md).


=== s520b (Opus, 2026-10-18): a SECOND member of the family ===
`(local $g) = ($g + 1);` -- a local in the LEFT list of an assignment whose RIGHT side reads the operand.  perl evaluates the right side first: in g=2 / g=1.  fd04c048 HOISTED it (`local $g; ($g) = ($g + 1)`) and the right side read the localized undef: in g=1 (silent wrong).  s520b (#3363) checks an assignment's right side like the tokens before the term when the term is in the left operand: a right side that names the operand or runs a call is not hoisted, so the shape is now this task's ANNOUNCED residue (`PCL: local in an unsupported expression position ... -- not localized`; in g=2 / g=2).  `@{local $x[0][0]} = 1` (an inert right side) still hoists.  Guard: Pl/t/local-term-01.t rows 20-21.  A lowering: `my @__t = (RHS); local OP; (OP) = @__t;` (list context kept).
subject: a `local` in a VOID expression position no lowering reaches is read without being localized (announced, ruling 4 of s519): the site-scan shapes
